title: ExtractionResult
description: Structured output contract for the ingestion LLM call. Deliberately domain-agnostic: this schema does not assume the user's work is about software projects, task management, or any specific field. Everything reduces to three generic primitives (declarative facts, episodic events, commitments) plus generic relationships between them. Product-specific behaviors (task sequencing, solution reuse) are expressed as *patterns over these primitives* at the retrieval layer, not as rigid required categories here — so the same schema can be run against an arbitrary real user's dictation corpus without silently dropping or misclassifying content that doesn't fit a narrower model.

capture_id.description: Foreign key back to the raw captures table row this extraction was run against. Passed in, echoed back for validation, not generated by the model.

extraction_status.description: Domain-agnostic gate: regardless of what the user's work is about, casual chatter, hypothetical brainstorming, secrets, and truncated captures are handled the same way. This is the one place the schema is intentionally strict.

discard_reason.description: Required (non-null) whenever extraction_status is not 'processed'. Feeds the Memory Inspector's rejected-ingestion log regardless of domain.

facts.description: Things stated to be true about an entity — a property, a number, a date, a status. Deliberately generic: a deadline, a budget figure, a person's role, a preference, and a technical spec value are all just facts with different attribute names. Do not add narrower fact sub-types; let 'attribute' carry the specificity.

events.description: Things that happened at a point in time — a decision, a problem encountered, a resolution found, a conversation, a correction. This is intentionally the broadest and least-constrained array, because a real, unfiltered dictation corpus is dominated by this category and its content is impossible to predict in advance.

commitments.description: Anything planned, promised, or owed — not limited to 'tasks' in a project-management sense. A promise to follow up with someone, an intention to revisit a decision, an owed deliverable, and a to-do item are all commitments. The only shared requirement across all of them is that status must never silently become 'done' without an explicit confirming statement from the user.

relationships.description: Generic links between any two mentions extracted above (facts, events, or commitments), used for ordering, solution-reuse, corrections, and any other connection the user states explicitly. One mechanism instead of several bespoke ones, so new kinds of connection don't require a schema change.

AsserterRole.description: Distinguishes the user's own stated belief/fact from something they're reporting someone else said. Domain-agnostic — applies equally to 'my manager said X' and 'the client mentioned Y'.

PrecisionClass.description: Whether a numeric/dated value is exact or a rounded spoken approximation. Exact values win at query time when both exist for the same attribute, regardless of domain.

entity_mention.description: Raw text mention of the entity this fact is about. Could be a project, a person, a document, a system, a place — anything. Resolved to a canonical entity_id downstream, not here.

entity_type.description: Free-text label for what kind of thing entity_mention refers to, e.g. 'project', 'person', 'document', 'system', 'place', 'deal'. Deliberately open rather than enum-constrained, since the extractor should describe what it actually sees rather than being forced into a fixed vocabulary designed around one workflow. Downstream code can normalize common values without the schema itself gatekeeping them.

attribute.description: The property being stated, e.g. 'deadline', 'budget', 'owner', 'status', 'preference'. Free text — this field, not entity_type, is what should carry domain specificity.

relative_time_expression.description: Original spoken/selected phrase for any date-like value, e.g. 'next Tuesday', 'effective immediately'. Retained for audit and for correctly anchoring selected-text relative language against the source document's authored date rather than the ingestion timestamp.

resolved_time.description: Absolute ISO-8601 resolution of relative_time_expression, computed at ingestion.

entity_mention.description: The entity this event concerns, if any. Optional because some events are self-contained (a general observation, a standalone decision) with no clear single entity.

event_type.description: Free-text label for what kind of thing happened. No fixed vocabulary — common values will likely include things like 'decision', 'problem_encountered', 'resolution_found', 'conversation', 'correction', 'observation', but the extractor should describe the real event rather than force-fitting it into a preset list. Retrieval logic can pattern-match on this field's text without the schema constraining what values are possible.

description.description: What actually happened, in enough detail to be useful on its own — this is the field that carries most of the informational weight for events, since event_type is deliberately loose.

asserter_role.description: Optional — populate when it's meaningful to distinguish the user's own action/observation from a third party's, null when not applicable.

commitment_mention.description: Short raw-text label for the commitment as the user referred to it — used as the join key for later mentions and for relationships referencing it. Not assumed to be a 'task' in any specific sense; could be a promise, a reminder, an owed follow-up, anything planned.

description.description: Fuller description of what is actually owed/planned, beyond the short mention label.

entity_mention.description: Parent entity this commitment relates to, if any (a project, a person, a deal). Optional — many commitments won't have one.

status.description: Defaults to open on first mention regardless of domain. Must never be 'done' unless status_confirmed_by_user is also true — this is the schema-level enforcement of never marking something finished on an assumption.

status_confirmed_by_user.description: True only for an explicit, unambiguous completion statement. Hedged language ('I'll probably get to that soon') must be extracted as status='in_progress' or 'open' with this false, never as done — regardless of what kind of commitment it is.

source_mention.description: The mention (from facts/events/commitments, this or a prior capture) that is the origin of the relationship — e.g. the earlier problem, the prerequisite commitment, the original fact being corrected.

target_mention.description: The mention that the relationship points to — e.g. the resolution, the dependent commitment, the corrected value.

relationship_type.description: Free-text label for the kind of connection, e.g. 'must_precede', 'resolves', 'corrects', 'relates_to', 'caused_by'. Deliberately open — this single mechanism covers task ordering, problem/solution linking, and self-correction candidates without needing a separate array for each, so new relationship kinds discovered in real data don't require a schema change.

reason.description: Why the connection holds, if the user stated one — surfaced back to the user when Kivi explains a suggested order or a reused solution.
